rules.title: Relocation payments for owner/relative move-in, demolition/permanent removal, temporary capital improvement, and substantial rehabilitation evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting for owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation amounts set by the Rent Board. The amount depends on the date the eviction notice is served. For notices served 3/01/26–2/28/27, the amounts are $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit. An additional $5,497.00 is due for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children.
rules.key_value: $8,245.00 per tenant; $24,733.00 max per unit; +$5,497.00 per elderly/disabled tenant or household with minor children (notices served 3/01/26–2/28/27)
rules.quoted_span: *The amount of relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions for less than 20 days is governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 and not by Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.
rules.coverage_text: Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in OR Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use OR Temporary Capital Improvement Work OR Substantial Rehabilitation
rules.exemptions: Relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 rather than Rent Ordinance Section 37.9C.
rules.interaction: For temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days, state law (Civil Code 1947.9) governs relocation amounts instead of the local ordinance. The local ordinance therefore does not displace the state rule in that case.
rules.conflict_note: The 2026-03-01 date is the start of the current rate period shown in the archive table, not an enactment date. Separate Ellis Act relocation rates ($11,110.05 per tenant; $33,330.13 max per unit; +$7,443.90 per elderly (62+) or disabled tenant for 3/01/26–2/28/27) appear only in table headings with no full-sentence support, so they are not extracted as a separate record.
